title: Hund’s rule and first ionization
hints: Relate pair repulsion to ease of removal.
solution: N has three singly occupied 2p orbitals. O has one pair in 2p, so removing an electron from that pair costs less energy.
statement:
Why is the first ionization energy of O lower than that of N?

[_]{a}

choices: Removing a paired O 2p electron reduces repulsion.
N has an extra principal shell.
explanations: O has a paired 2p orbital, and N has three singly occupied 2p orbitals.
O has more protons than N.
